Starting today, WhatsApp Web users can view, inspect, and annotate PDF files directly within their chats, without leaving the messaging interface. Details below.

Adobe Acrobat is now available on WhatsApp Web

Previously, when a user received a PDF file on WhatsApp, they had to download it before opening it, and the app did not include any built-in viewing or annotation tools.

Adobe announced today that its Acrobat PDF tools are now integrated directly into WhatsApp Web and the WhatsApp Windows app, allowing users to open, view, and annotate documents without downloading the file or leaving the chat window.

Adobe stated that, in addition to standard PDF files, this integration also supports password-protected documents, and that files shared in chats remain protected by WhatsApp's end-to-end encryption, meaning "only the members of the chat can read them," Adobe pointed out.

Adobe noted that this integration reflects the growing number of users who use WhatsApp on a large screen to handle tasks such as reviewing contracts, invoices, forms, and assignments, and also represents its broader strategy of bringing Acrobat's PDF tools to the platforms where users do their everyday work, "such as Chrome, Microsoft 365 and Copilot, ChatGPT, Workday, and others."
